states.name: history_reg
states.meaning: 32-bit speculative global branch history register; predict_history[0] is the direction of the youngest branch and older branches are at higher bit positions.
states.update_time: asynchronously to 0 when areset is high; otherwise at posedge clk when train_mispredicted is high or when predict_valid is high with no train_mispredicted

rules.condition: areset == 1; reset overrides all clocked prediction/training updates and forces predict_history to 0.
rules.spec_quote: areset is a positive edge triggered asynchronous reset that resets the history counter to zero.

rules.condition: areset == 0 && train_mispredicted == 1; at posedge clk, load with history after the mispredicted branch. With 32-bit truncation, new predict_history = ((train_history << 1) | train_taken) & 0xFFFFFFFF. This takes precedence over predict_valid.
rules.spec_quote: load the branch history register with the history after the completion of the mispredicted branch.

rules.condition: areset == 0 && train_mispredicted == 0 && predict_valid == 1; at posedge clk, shift in predict_taken at the LSB side: new predict_history = ((old_predict_history << 1) | predict_taken) & 0xFFFFFFFF.
rules.spec_quote: shift in predict_taken from the LSB side

rules.condition: areset == 0 && train_mispredicted == 0 && predict_valid == 0; at posedge clk, no branch-history update occurs and predict_history holds its previous value.
rules.spec_quote: predict_history is the value of the branch history register.

reset.name: areset
reset.first_released_cycle: the first sampled posedge with areset low; normal clocked updates may occur on that edge, otherwise the history remains at its current value.

mid: Optional mid-cycle input changes occur after sampling and before the next sampled edge; they are used only for the next row/edge and do not change the already sampled predict_history.

uncertain.note: The specification says to load a 32-bit register with train_history concatenated with train_taken, but does not explicitly state which bit is discarded when forming the 32-bit result. This contract assumes the standard shift-in-at-LSB truncation.
candidates: new = ((train_history >> 1) | (train_taken << 31)) & 0xFFFFFFFF; shift train_taken into the MSB side
new = train_history; ignore the extra train_taken bit because the register is already 32 bits
